newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Primary aluminium demand to rise in 97 - Pechiney.
newsitem.headline: Primary aluminium demand to rise in 97 - Pechiney.

text.p: The head of the aluminium division of Pechiney International SA said on Tuesday he expected primary aluminium demand to rise this year, driven by stronger European economic growth.

"There is no reason why we should not experience a reasonable level of consumption growth this year. Relatively low inventories and more comfortable LME prices are auspicious," Bernard Legrand said in a speech to the Organisation of European Aluminium Refiners and Smelters.
Global aluminium demand fell one percent in 1996 to 17.7 million tonnes but low European interest rates and a stronger dollar formed a favourable economic backdrop this year, Legrand said.
"In recent weeks the market for aluminium has continued to strengthen, showing a higher physical demand," he continued.
Three months aluminium touched a nine-month high of $1,663 on the LME on Tuesday after a bigger than expected inventory decline.

Legrand predicted aluminium would play an increasingly important role in the car and aeronautical industries thanks to its unique properties of high strength, corrosion resistance and complete recyclability.
He also forecast long-term demand growth from the expanding economies of Asia, China and Russia. --Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
